answer: Every applicant must fire a one-off glass panel whose pigment swirl and opal inlay are photographed, then strike the panel so its echo is recorded as a fingerprint; the registry accepts the panel only when pigment, opal and echo all match the submitted record. Forging one panel costs $60 in glass and firing plus $15 for certification, so 100 fake identities burn $7,500 and leave 100 useless panels, since each panel's swirl and echo are unique.
